## What the plan builds

One new check, **`c50`**, in `scripts/verify_plan.py`. Plain reading: when a plan says it will EDIT an exact piece of text in a workflow-surface file (a `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`, agents, rules, hooks, `CLAUDE.md`, `workflow.yaml`), the check finds every file under `tests/` that ASSERTS on that exact text and WARNs for each such test file the plan did not list as an edit target. `c50` is the next free id (the registry topped out at `c49`).

This mechanizes the #1948 catch. Plan v2 for #1948 declared an edit to the SKILL.md inline-gate single-flight probe pattern without listing `tests/test_issue_skill_gate_single_flight.py`, whose line ~104-106 asserted the exact old literal — which made that plan's own acceptance criterion ("Step 9c compare exit 0") deterministically unsatisfiable as scoped. Only the Claude critic caught it.

No overlap with existing pin logic: `c31`, the #1679 arm, and the pin-form satisfiers all run the INVERSE direction (a plan must DECLARE a pin for prose it ADDS). None searches `tests/` for pins on a plan-EDITED literal.

## Verdict class: WARN-only, calibrated on measurement

The planner prototyped the check and swept it over all **3,713** live plan files (as of the 2026-08-08 sweep). Final design fires on **393 (10.6%)** — the same band as `c31`'s accepted #1557 calibration (328/3,024 ≈ 11%), which the critic independently verified as an apt comparison (same kind scope, same verdict class, same corpus, same consequence). Design iterations measured 1,848 → 833 → 437 → 393 as discriminators landed. FAIL-class at that fire rate is the #1388 fleet-wedge shape, so the check WARNs. Note 10.6% is a FIRE rate, not a false-positive rate; a hand-inspected sample of 10 mixed genuine under-listing (#815, #1032, #1138) with vocabulary false positives (`America/Los_Angeles`, `AUTO-GENERATED`) — acceptance requires a stratified ~30-50-plan classification into `genuine under-listing` | `citation-context FP` | `vocabulary FP`, recorded in the calibration comment.

## Incident replay: FIRES

Replayed against incident-time file states (`git show b2bf75ee36~1`), c50 WARNs naming `tests/test_issue_skill_gate_single_flight.py` via the `issue-<N>-inline-payload.txt` literal. The removal-vocabulary tier is proven load-bearing by ablation — the design without it reads PASS — so the replay can FAIL a wrong design; it is a test, not a fit to one known case.
